objective: Port netty-handler 4.2.19.Final to Netty.NET.Handler with the original names, structure, comments and tests. The nine packages other than io.netty.handler.ssl came first (2026-11-23); io.netty.handler.ssl followed on 2026-11-24 on System.Net.Security.SslStream per the owner's design (docs/handler-ssl-design.md).

ownerDecisions: Project, folder and assembly names are the namespace root of the module (owner decision 2026-11-19, see docs/codec-base-porting.md): each codec module takes the namespace of its main package, and the tests use <project>.Tests like the other test projects.

Owner decisions 2026-11-19 for the codec modules that only need codec-base: one project per Maven module; codec-socks is Netty.NET.Handler.Codec.Socks (its Maven and JPMS name) and holds the socks and socksx namespaces; haproxy is HAProxy (the casing of the Java types in that package); socksx, v4 and v5 are Socksx, V4 and V5.

Owner decisions 2026-11-23: the project is Netty.NET.Handler (namespace root of io.netty.handler, decided 2026-11-19); sub-packages become Netty.NET.Handler.Address/Flow/Flush/IpFilter/Logging/Pcap/Stream/Timeout/Traffic (ipfilter takes the casing of its Java types IpFilterRule/IpSubnetFilter, as haproxy became HAProxy); the non-ssl packages are ported before ssl.

Owner decisions 2026-11-24: io.netty.handler.ssl and io.netty.handler.ssl.util become Netty.NET.Handler.Ssl and Netty.NET.Handler.Ssl.Util (folders Ssl/ and Ssl/Util/); SslHandler runs on SslStream behind a record-aligned mediation stream, the SSLEngine constructors take the BCL authentication options, OpenSSL/Bouncy Castle/Conscrypt units are library-not-ported (docs/handler-ssl-design.md).

review.scope: Abstract ChannelOutboundHandlerAdapter. The outbound operations take the CancellationToken in place of the ChannelPromise and return the Task that replaces it (docs/codec-base-porting.md, Outbound operations); SocketAddress is EndPoint. The final connect(...) is a sealed override of ConnectAsync: promise.setFailure(e) after localAddress()/remoteAddress() throw is the returned faulted Task, and the listener on ctx.connect(...) that removes the handler after a successful connect is a synchronous continuation (it runs at once when the connect already completed, as a listener added to a done future). localAddress(...)/remoteAddress(...) are protected virtual LocalAddress/RemoteAddress; throws Exception has no C# counterpart.

@Sharable is [Sharable]. AddressResolverGroup<? extends SocketAddress> has no C# wildcard, a constructor cannot declare its own type parameter and a generic class is invariant (variance is limited to generic interfaces and delegates), so the wildcard is the class type parameter: ResolveAddressHandler<T> where T : EndPoint accepts any AddressResolverGroup<T> (DefaultAddressResolverGroup is AddressResolverGroup<IPEndPoint>), as Transport made Bootstrap.resolver(AddressResolverGroup<?>) the generic method Resolver<T>. The outbound operations take the CancellationToken in place of the ChannelPromise and return the Task that replaces it (docs/codec-base-porting.md, Outbound operations); SocketAddress is EndPoint. On the resolution path the promise is a TaskCompletionSource: the FutureListener is a synchronous continuation of the resolve Task, future.cause() != null (a faulted or cancelled Task) is copied with TrySetFromTask, and ctx.connect(future.getNow(), localAddress, promise) copies the connect Task into it (docs/common-task-composition.md); the handler is removed after the connect is started, as in the source.

review.scope: T extends SocketAddress is T : EndPoint; ChannelFuture is Task. The unchecked (T) cast of remoteAddress() is erased in Java, and the bridge method of a narrower accept(...) override checks the type inside the try, so a mismatch closes the channel; the checked C# cast is therefore made inside the try for the same outcome. catch (Throwable) is catch (Exception) and PlatformDependent.throwException(cause) is throw; (the unreachable "return true" after it is not repeated). ChannelFutureListener.CLOSE on the channelRejected(...) future is a synchronous continuation that closes ctx.Channel (a Task has no channel), as codec-base MessageAggregator does. IllegalStateException is InvalidOperationException; the discarded ctx.close() Tasks are not observed.
Interface with the I prefix; matches(InetSocketAddress) is Matches(IPEndPoint) and ruleType() is the method RuleType().

Simple Java enum: a C# enum with the Java constant names. Being a value type it cannot be null, so checkNotNull(ruleType, "ruleType") in IpSubnetFilterRule has no counterpart and IpSubnetFilter keeps its null "no common rule type" state in IpFilterRuleType?.

@Sharable is [Sharable]. InetAddress is IPAddress and InetSocketAddress is IPEndPoint (docs/codec-dns-porting.md); instanceof Inet4Address/Inet6Address is AddressFamily.InterNetwork/InterNetworkV6 (the NIO channels report the IPv4 peers of dual-mode sockets in IPv4 form, AbstractNioChannel.Normalize). List<IpSubnetFilterRule> is IList<IpSubnetFilterRule> (an array is one, as Arrays.asList makes it a List); the IpFilterRuleType fields that may be null are IpFilterRuleType?. Arrays.binarySearch(rules, address, comparator) is Array.BinarySearch<object> (the CLR search also passes the array element first and returns a negative value when the address is in no rule). Collections.sort is stable and List.Sort is not, so sortAndFilter iterates the stable Enumerable.OrderBy with the anonymous Comparator as a Comparison wrapped by Comparer<T>.Create; that keeps the Java order of equal rules and so the parent named in the overlap message. Iterator hasNext()/next() are MoveNext()/Current, IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException and toArray(new IpSubnetFilterRule[0]) is ToArray(). The tests reach the protected accept(...) through Java package access; C# protected access is limited to derived classes, so the internal forwarder InvokeAccept serves the friend test assembly, as MessageToMessageDecoder.InvokeDecode in codec-base.

Sealed class implementing IIpFilterRule and IComparable<IpSubnetFilterRule>; the package-private members (getIpAddress(), getFilterRule(), compareTo(InetSocketAddress), contains(...)) are internal. InetAddress is IPAddress and InetSocketAddress is IPEndPoint (docs/codec-dns-porting.md); instanceof Inet4Address/Inet6Address is AddressFamily.InterNetwork/InterNetworkV6 (the NIO channels report the IPv4 peers of dual-mode sockets in IPv4 form, AbstractNioChannel.Normalize). SocketUtils.addressByName (InetAddress.getByName) is the DefaultNameResolver lookup that Transport AbstractBootstrap uses for the same call (JDK literal rules, an IPv4-mapped literal becomes IPv4, UnknownHostException is SocketException), so catch (UnknownHostException) is catch (SocketException); an invalid host name that Dns rejects with ArgumentException is not wrapped and stays an ArgumentException. ipAddressWithCidr.split("/") drops trailing empty strings in Java, so they are removed after string.Split. Integer.parseInt is int.Parse with a leading sign and the invariant culture; its NumberFormatException (an IllegalArgumentException subclass) is FormatException/OverflowException, the mapping of codec-base CharSequenceValueConverter. InetAddress.getHostAddress() of the InetAddress constructor keeps the JDK text: the dotted quad for IPv4 and, for IPv6, eight uncompressed hex groups plus "%scope" (OpenJDK numericToTextFormat), while IPAddress.ToString() compresses with "::"; a scope id of 0 counts as none. The private members of the nested Ip4SubnetFilterRule/Ip6SubnetFilterRule that the enclosing class reads are internal (C# does not open them to the outer class). Byte/sign: Java int and C# int are both signed 32-bit, so NetUtil.Ipv4AddressToInt, the masks, compareInt(x ^ MIN_VALUE, ...) and (int) (-1L << 32 - cidrPrefix) (shift counts masked to 6/5 bits, unchecked narrowing) give the Java values; java.math.BigInteger is System.Numerics.BigInteger, whose & and << use the same two's-complement semantics, and new BigInteger(1, octets) is new BigInteger(octets, isUnsigned: true, isBigEndian: true) over GetAddressBytes() (network order). String.format("%d") is the invariant-culture text; the IPv6 locals of contains(...) are parent6/child6 (CS0136).

Internal sealed class with the private constructor and the internal static INSTANCE; Comparator<Object> is IComparer<object>. Array.BinarySearch calls comparer.Compare(array[i], value) (ArraySortHelper), so o1 is the rule and o2 the IPEndPoint, as in Arrays.binarySearch.

@ChannelHandler.Sharable is [Sharable]. ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet() is a ConcurrentDictionary<IPAddress, bool> used as a set (add is TryAdd, which returns false if the key exists; remove is TryRemove); IPAddress.Equals compares the address as InetAddress.equals does. review.scope: Generic subclass of SslClientHelloHandler<T>. The handshake timeout ScheduledFuture is the CancellationTokenSource of ctx.Executor.ScheduleAsync (cancel(false) is Cancel()), as IdleStateHandler keeps its timeouts; the anonymous Runnable is a lambda; ctx.close() discards the CloseAsync Task. extractSniHostname decodes the host name with Encoding.Latin1, because ByteBuf.toString(..., US_ASCII) takes ByteBufUtil.decodeString's fast path new String(array, 0, offset, len), which maps every octet to (char) (b & 0xff) (Encoding.ASCII would give '?' above 127), and lower-cases with ToLowerInvariant (Locale.US has no special casing). review.scope: The SSL/TLS implementation is SslStream. The SSLContext is replaced by the trust and key material SslStream takes per connection (X509ChainPolicy or RemoteCertificateValidationCallback; SslStreamCertificateContext, built once per context so Linux servers can resume sessions, or a selection callback). The public constructors that take a pre-configured SSLContext and context() are not ported (two @Deprecated ones name the SSLContext constructor); the package-private constructor is the internal constructor with the SSLContext replaced by that material and without the ResumptionController, and the internal factories NewJdkSslServerContext/NewJdkSslClientContext do what the @Deprecated JdkSslServerContext/JdkSslClientContext constructors did for the builder (trust certificates -> buildTrustManagerFactory, key -> buildKeyManagerFactory, the default TrustManagerFactory is the system trust of a null CertificateChainPolicy, "key, keyManagerFactory" NullPointerException as ArgumentNullException, failures wrapped in AuthenticationException "failed to initialize the server/client-side SSL context", client ClientAuth.NONE and startTls false as in the source; session cache size/timeout and SecureRandom have no option). The JCA Provider comparison has only the default branch (the other one probes a non-default provider's engine; its comments are recorded). Defaults: DEFAULT_PROTOCOLS from the TLS 1.3 probe of SslUtils plus TLSv1.2 (SslStream has no query for the OS defaults; the SslStream of a context without configured protocols uses SslProtocols.None, the recommended OS choice), SUPPORTED_CIPHERS are the TlsCipherSuite names (IANA names = JSSE names; the IBM J9 "SSL_" probe through SSLEngine.setEnabledCipherSuites is not ported, comments recorded), DEFAULT_CIPHERS as in the source with the supported names as fallback for engine.getEnabledCipherSuites(); unmodifiable collections are ReadOnlySet/ReadOnlyCollection, LinkedHashSet HashSet. sessionContext() (SSLSessionContext) is not ported; newEngine x2 + configureAndWrapEngine become the NewHandler overrides that build a fresh SslClientAuthenticationOptions/SslServerAuthenticationOptions per handler: setEnabledCipherSuites is a CipherSuitesPolicy only when cipher suites were configured (unknown name: ArgumentException "Unsupported CipherSuite", Windows/Android: PlatformNotSupportedException), setEnabledProtocols EnabledSslProtocols (unknown name: ArgumentException; SSLv2Hello ignored; legacy names map to the obsolete values), setWant/NeedClientAuth ClientCertificateRequired with the "exhaustive cases" switch kept, configureSSLParameters TargetHost = first SNI server name else peer host, the ALPN wrapper ApplicationProtocols. The remote certificate decision (a CLR-only callback, installed only when needed) follows JSSE: no certificate -> a client fails, a server accepts unless REQUIRE; endpoint identification null -> RemoteCertificateNameMismatch cleared; a TrustManager callback decides like an X509ExtendedTrustManager; else no SslPolicyErrors. toNegotiator keeps its switch and NotSupportedException texts and returns a private IApplicationProtocolNegotiator (the JDK negotiator types are @Deprecated, not ported); FATAL_ALERT vs NO_ADVERTISE/ACCEPT has no SslStream option. buildKeyManagerFactory x4 return SslStreamCertificateContext; the two "@deprecated will be removed." overloads name no replacement and have [Obsolete("will be removed.")]; Security.getProperty is the fallback "SunX509".

review.scope: ByteToMessageDecoder with the Java structure; List<Object> out is IList<object> @out and the decode parameter keeps its Java name context. SslHandler.isEncrypted(in, false) is the static SslHandler.IsEncrypted of the ssl-handler port. ReferenceCountUtil.safeRelease(sslHandler.engine()) for a handler that did not reach the pipeline is the Dispose of the SslStream engine of the handler (the internal SslHandler.Engine(); SslStream.Dispose "Releases the unmanaged resources used by the SslStream"); the try/finally and its comments are kept.

Internal interface IPemEncoded : IByteBufHolder with IsSensitive(); the covariant re-declarations of copy/duplicate/retainedDuplicate/replace/retain/touch are inherited from IByteBufHolder (owner decision 2026-11-19, docs/transport-porting.md Decisions), so callers cast their results.

PrivateKey is AsymmetricAlgorithm in this port (ssl design decision 3), an abstract class, and the type already derives from AbstractReferenceCounted, so it is a public sealed reference-counted holder of the PEM bytes implementing IPemEncoded, not an AsymmetricAlgorithm. The IByteBufHolder members (copy/duplicate/retainedDuplicate/replace returning the own type, covariant retain/touch overrides and explicit IByteBufHolder implementations) follow codec-memcache DefaultMemcacheContent; content() is the Content property, which checks the reference count and throws the Common IllegalReferenceCountException. Of the Key members, getFormat() (a value) is GetFormat(); getEncoded() and getAlgorithm(), which only throw UnsupportedOperationException and have no base to implement, are not ported (no comments). Destroyable destroy()/isDestroyed() are Destroy()/IsDestroyed() with their Javadoc. toPEM(allocator, useDirect, PrivateKey) takes object: an IPemEncoded takes the shortcut, an AsymmetricAlgorithm is encoded with ExportPkcs8PrivateKey (PKCS #8, what getEncoded() returns) and any other object is the getEncoded() == null case. It only feeds the library-not-ported OpenSSL context. serialVersionUID has no counterpart.

Internal static class (The source's private constructor only prevents instantiation, so the class is static.) File is FileInfo and InputStream is System.IO.Stream; CertificateException and KeyException (GeneralSecurityException) are CryptographicException with the same messages, as pkitesting maps them. FileInputStream reports a missing, directory or unreadable file as FileNotFoundException (an IOException), while FileInfo.OpenRead() throws UnauthorizedAccessException for a read-only name or directory, so both map to the "could not find" exceptions. Pattern/Matcher are Regex/Match: find(start) is Match(input, start), end() is Index + Length, usePattern switches the Regex used at the kept position. The content is decoded with Encoding.ASCII ('?' where Java puts U+FFFD above 127; no pattern tells them apart), so the .NET \s matches Java's ASCII \s, and CASE_INSENSITIVE (US-ASCII only) is the explicit class [a-zA-Z0-9+/=]. readContent reads to the end of the stream (0, Java -1) into a MemoryStream.

Internal AbstractReferenceCounted holder implementing IPemEncoded. The IByteBufHolder members (copy/duplicate/retainedDuplicate/replace returning the own type, covariant retain/touch overrides and explicit IByteBufHolder implementations) follow codec-memcache DefaultMemcacheContent; content() is the Content property, which checks the reference count and throws the Common IllegalReferenceCountException. deallocate() zeroes a sensitive value through SslUtils.Zeroout before releasing it.

X509Certificate is X509Certificate2 (ssl design decision 3), whose instances always hold a parsed certificate (data-loading constructors obsolete, X509CertificateLoader instead), while this class holds unvalidated PEM bytes that may be a whole chain; so it is a public sealed reference-counted holder implementing IPemEncoded, not an X509Certificate2. The 25 X509Certificate overrides that only throw UnsupportedOperationException have no base to implement and are not ported (no comments). refCnt/retain/release/touch forward to the content; The IByteBufHolder members (copy/duplicate/retainedDuplicate/replace returning the own type, covariant retain/touch overrides and explicit IByteBufHolder implementations) follow codec-memcache DefaultMemcacheContent; content() is the Content property, which checks the reference count and throws the Common IllegalReferenceCountException. equals/hashCode/toString are Equals/GetHashCode/ToString (UTF-8). toPEM(allocator, useDirect, X509Certificate...) takes params object[]: IPemEncoded elements are appended as PEM, BCL X509Certificate elements are encoded from GetRawCertData() (DER, what getEncoded() returns), a null element is rejected with the Arrays.toString text; CertificateEncodingException has no counterpart. It only feeds the library-not-ported OpenSSL context.

Internal sealed class with the private constructor and its Javadoc. javax.crypto.Mac is IncrementalHash.CreateHMAC (getMacLength() HashLengthInBytes, doFinal AppendData + GetHashAndReset); the JCA Mac name (case-insensitive, "HmacSHA256") gives the case-sensitive BCL hash name after the "Hmac" prefix, upper-cased; a name the BCL does not know fails with CryptographicException, which becomes the IllegalArgumentException (ArgumentException) "Could not find algo", as a missing JCA algorithm does (HmacSHA224 and HmacSHA512/224 are such names). SecretKeySpec rejects an empty key, which the BCL allows, so that check follows the algorithm lookup as in the source. GeneralSecurityException is CryptographicException; Arrays.copyOf and System.arraycopy are Array.Copy.

review.scope: Internal static class (The source's private constructor only prevents instantiation, so the class is static.) java.util.regex.Pattern is Regex: Matcher.matches() is a match of the pattern wrapped in \A(?:...)\z, replaceFirst is Replace(input, replacement, 1), group(n) of a group that did not take part is null (read through Group()), and the Java "." is written as the class without the Java line terminators (\n, \r, \u0085, \u2028, \u2029) because the .NET "." only excludes \n. toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT) is ToUpperInvariant() and equalsIgnoreCase is an OrdinalIgnoreCase comparison, which agree with Java on the ASCII OpenSSL names.

Sealed subclass with the three constructors; hostname() is Hostname(). toString() keeps the Java text: a null hostname prints "null" (C# string concatenation would print nothing) and the cause is Throwable.toString().

Mapping is Func<string, SslContext> and AsyncMapping IAsyncMapping<string, SslContext> (MapAsync returns a provider-owned Task; docs/common-clr-design.md "Native synchronous domain selection", docs/common-native-async-mapping.md); Func is covariant in its result and IAsyncMapping contravariant in its input, Task<T> is invariant, and DomainNameMapping<? extends SslContext> is DomainNameMapping<SslContext> whose Map method is the Func. lookup is mapping.MapAsync(hostname) (AbstractSniHandler continues on the executor of the channelexecutor); onLookupComplete reads IsCompletedSuccessfully/Result and the faulted or cancelled cause (as AbstractSniHandler), wraps it in DecoderException (java.lang.Error has no CLR counterpart, so its rethrow is not ported) and resets the selection with catch (Exception)/throw;. AsyncMappingAdapter uses Task.FromResult/FromException. SslHandler.class.getName() is typeof(SslHandler).FullName. ReferenceCountUtil.safeRelease(sslHandler.engine()) for a handler that did not reach the pipeline is the Dispose of the SslStream engine of the handler (the internal SslHandler.Engine(); SslStream.Dispose "Releases the unmanaged resources used by the SslStream"); the try/finally and its comments are kept. hostname()/sslContext() are Hostname()/SslContext().

ByteToMessageDecoder implementing IChannelOutboundHandler with the Java outbound overrides as virtual Task-returning members (ChannelPromise is the CancellationToken/Task pair, SocketAddress is EndPoint), as codec-base DatagramPacketEncoder forwards them. Future<T> is Task<T>: isDone() is IsCompleted and the FutureListener is a continuation on IdleStateHandler.ExecutorTaskScheduler over the context, which runs it at once on the event loop and otherwise hands it to the executor (DefaultPromise.notifyListeners policy). decode keeps the record and fragment logic; the switch fall-through into default is goto default; getUnsignedByte is GetByte (unsigned System.Byte); catch (Throwable) after catch (Exception) has no counterpart and PlatformDependent.throwException is throw;. MAX_CLIENT_HELLO_LENGTH and DEFAULT_MAX_CLIENT_HELLO_LENGTH are constants of the generic class.

The SSLEngine of the Javadoc is the SslStream that SslHandler drives; serialVersionUID has no counterpart.

notApplicable.sourceComment:
Creates a new {@link SslHandler}.

If {@link SslProvider#OPENSSL_REFCNT} is used then the returned {@link SslHandler} will release the engine that is wrapped. If the returned {@link SslHandler} is not inserted into a pipeline then you may leak native memory!

Beware: the underlying generated {@link SSLEngine} won't have hostname verification enabled by default. If you create {@link SslHandler} for the client side and want proper security, we advice that you configure the {@link SSLEngine} (see {@link javax.net.ssl.SSLParameters#setEndpointIdentificationAlgorithm(String)}): 

 SSLEngine sslEngine = sslHandler.engine(); SSLParameters sslParameters = sslEngine.getSSLParameters(); // only available since Java 7 sslParameters.setEndpointIdentificationAlgorithm("HTTPS"); sslEngine.setSSLParameters(sslParameters);

The underlying {@link SSLEngine} may not follow the restrictions imposed by the SSLEngine javadocs which limits wrap/unwrap to operate on a single SSL/TLS packet. @param alloc If supported by the SSLEngine then the SSLEngine will use this to allocate ByteBuf objects. @param delegatedTaskExecutor the {@link Executor} that will be used to execute tasks that are returned by {@link SSLEngine#getDelegatedTask()}. @return a new {@link SslHandler}
notApplicable.reason: The Executor runs the tasks of SSLEngine.getDelegatedTask(); SslStream has no delegated tasks (it runs certificate callbacks and crypto inline, members of SslStream), so the overloads have no counterpart.

review.scope: Abstract class with the public API kept where it has a BCL counterpart. Owner decision 2026-11-24 (docs/handler-ssl-design.md, decision 2): no SSLEngine facade; SslStream is the engine and the per-handler SslClientAuthenticationOptions/SslServerAuthenticationOptions replace the SSLEngine a context creates. So newEngine(alloc) and newEngine(alloc, peerHost, peerPort) and sessionContext() are not ported, and the protected newHandler(alloc, startTls) and newHandler(alloc, peerHost, peerPort, startTls), whose bodies only wrapped newEngine in an SslHandler, are protected internal abstract (JdkSslContext builds a fresh SslClientAuthenticationOptions/SslServerAuthenticationOptions per handler; DelegatingSslContext calls them on another context, which Java's package access allows). sessionCacheSize()/sessionTimeout() only read the SSLSessionContext and SslStream has no session cache size or timeout (design Known differences): not ported. The newHandler overloads that take an Executor pass it to SSLEngine.getDelegatedTask(); SslStream has no delegated tasks (it runs certificate callbacks and crypto inline), so they are not ported (the ssl-handler agent decides the SslHandler side; reported to the lead). The @Deprecated newServerContext/newClientContext overloads and nextProtocols() are not ported (owner rule 2026-11-16); the package-private newServerContext(..., keyStore), toApplicationProtocolConfig, toPrivateKeyInternal and toX509CertificatesInternal only serve those, the @Deprecated JdkSslClientContext/JdkSslServerContext or the OpenSSL contexts and are not ported (only the first has a comment). newServerContextInternal/newClientContextInternal (x2) keep their flow without the JCA Provider and the library-not-ported OpenSslCredential list, take the trust/key material as BCL types (X509Certificate2[], X509ChainPolicy, RemoteCertificateValidationCallback, AsymmetricAlgorithm, SslStreamCertificateContext, Server/LocalCertificateSelectionCallback, RandomNumberGenerator), keep the "OCSP is not supported" check and build the JDK context through JdkSslContext.NewJdkSslServerContext/NewJdkSslClientContext (what the deprecated subclasses built); OPENSSL/OPENSSL_REFCNT throw NotSupportedException (OpenSsl unavailable) and an unexpected provider UnreachableException. defaultProvider() is JDK (OpenSsl.isAvailable() is false). defaultEndpointVerificationAlgorithm is protected internal (the builder reads it, Java protected admits the package) and is set in an explicit static constructor (equalsIgnoreCase is OrdinalIgnoreCase); X509_CERT_FACTORY (only the OpenSSL code uses it) is the static X509CertificateLoader, ALIAS has no PKCS #12 counterpart, the ResumptionController field/constructor are not ported. attributes() is IAttributeMap/DefaultAttributeMap. Key and certificate helpers (protected internal, as tests reach them through package access): toX509Certificates(File/InputStream) load each PemReader DER block with X509CertificateLoader.LoadCertificate; toPrivateKey(File/InputStream, password[, tryBouncyCastle]) replaces the library-not-ported Bouncy Castle first attempt with the BCL PEM importers (ImportFromPem/ImportFromEncryptedPem on RSA, DSA, ECDsa; null when none reads the key, as BouncyCastlePemReader returns null), keeps mark/reset as CanSeek/Position with a MemoryStream for streams that cannot seek, and falls back to getPrivateKeyFromByteBuffer, whose KeyFactory RSA/DSA/EC are ImportPkcs8PrivateKey on RSA/DSA/ECDsa ("Neither RSA, DSA nor EC worked"). generateKeySpec (@Deprecated without @deprecated text) is ported with [Obsolete] returning the PKCS #8 bytes (PKCS8EncodedKeySpec): the BCL decrypts an EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo only while importing it, so it imports into RSA/DSA/ECDsa and exports the decrypted PKCS #8; getPBEAlgorithm (EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo/AlgorithmParameters) is not ported. Measured: every PKCS #8 test key (PBES2 AES/3DES, PKCS#12 PBE-SHA1-3DES, PBES1-MD5-DES, plain) and unencrypted PKCS #1 RSA load; legacy "Proc-Type: 4,ENCRYPTED" PKCS #1 and PKCS #1 DSA keys do not (Bouncy Castle reads them in Java). buildKeyStore returns the PKCS #12 bytes of the leaf combined with the key (CopyWithPrivateKey) plus the chain, as X509Bundle.ToKeyStore; the key store type only selects the JCA KeyStore implementation and is not used. buildTrustManagerFactory returns an X509ChainPolicy (CustomRootTrust, CustomTrustStore = the certificates, RevocationMode NoCheck), re-initializing a given policy as init(KeyStore) re-initializes a factory; the File/TrustManagerFactory overload (@Deprecated without text) has [Obsolete]. buildKeyManagerFactory returns an SslStreamCertificateContext created from the PKCS #12 round trip (persisted key, offline), as X509Bundle.ToKeyManagerFactory; the JCA key algorithm and the given kmf (which only select the factory algorithm/provider) are not used. CertificateException/KeyException/InvalidKeySpecException are CryptographicException, SSLException AuthenticationException, File FileInfo, InputStream System.IO.Stream.

review.scope: Sealed class keeping the fluent API with BCL parameter types (owner decision 3, as pkitesting X509Bundle maps them): PrivateKey AsymmetricAlgorithm, X509Certificate X509Certificate2, File FileInfo, InputStream System.IO.Stream, Iterable IEnumerable, TrustManagerFactory X509ChainPolicy (CertificateChainPolicy), TrustManager RemoteCertificateValidationCallback, KeyManagerFactory SslStreamCertificateContext (Server/ClientCertificateContext), KeyManager ServerCertificateSelectionCallback (server) or LocalCertificateSelectionCallback (client; a new KeyManager(LocalCertificateSelectionCallback) overload, as the BCL has two delegate types where a JCA KeyManager serves both sides), SecureRandom RandomNumberGenerator, SNIServerName the host name string (only SNIHostName is supported; SslStream sends TargetHost as SNI), Map.Entry[] KeyValuePair<SslContextOption, object>[], KeyStore.getDefaultType() "PKCS12". The callbacks are kept in their own fields next to the factory fields (the JCA TrustManagerFactoryWrapper/KeyManagerFactoryWrapper are jvm-only-replaced), and setting one clears the others as setting a factory clears the certificates. sslContextProvider(Provider) has no counterpart (JCA Provider) and addCredential/addCredentials are library-not-ported (OpenSslCredential); their comments are recorded. sessionCacheSize/sessionTimeout/secureRandom are kept and not applied (no SslStream option); ciphers(...) applies a CipherSuitesPolicy, which Windows and Android do not support, so a context with configured cipher suites fails in newHandler there (PlatformNotSupportedException); endpointIdentificationAlgorithm keeps SslStream's single host name check for any non-null algorithm ("HTTPS", "LDAPS") and clears it for null. Inside the class the methods SslProvider/ClientAuth/ApplicationProtocolConfig hide the same-named types in expressions, so those are qualified. ClientAuth is a value type (no checkNotNull); IllegalArgumentException is ArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException NotSupportedException.

Java keeps one ConstantPool<SslContextOption<Object>> and casts its constants unchecked to any T, which erasure permits; a C# generic class has static fields per closed type and its instances are not convertible between type arguments. So the file holds a non-generic abstract SslContextOption (AbstractConstant base, the pool as a ConcurrentDictionary from name to option, valueOf/exists as the static ValueOf<T>/Exists, the shared id counter) and SslContextOption<T> with the private (id, name) constructor (internal, for the pool), the protected (name) constructor and the virtual Validate(T), as Common AttributeKey keeps its registry. ValueOf<U> of a name first created for another T throws ArgumentException where Java returns the same object. Class.getName() is Type.FullName as in ConstantPool. checkNotNull(value) is written out because T may be a value type.

review.scope: Public class SslHandler : ByteToMessageDecoder, IChannelOutboundHandler on System.Net.Security.SslStream (owner decisions 2026-11-24, docs/handler-ssl-design.md). The Java structure, fields, state flags, method order, futures, timeouts, events and exception paths are kept; decode(...) still cuts records with SslUtils.getEncryptedPacketLength (NotSslRecordException), and only the SSLEngine calls are replaced by private Engine* methods (wrap/unwrap/beginHandshake/getHandshakeStatus/closeOutbound/closeInbound/isInboundDone/getUseClientMode) that return an EngineResult with SSLEngineResult's Status/HandshakeStatus, so the wrap, wrapNonAppData, wrapMultiple and unwrap loops keep their Java shape. SslStream reads and writes a private nested MediationStream (CLR-only helper, no manifest entry): EngineUnwrap pushes one whole record into SslStream's pending read, which completes inline (ManualResetValueTaskSourceCore without RunContinuationsAsynchronously), so the handshake, certificate callbacks and reads run inside the call on the event loop; RunEngine clears a SynchronizationContext and leaves a foreign TaskScheduler (Task.RunSynchronously on the default scheduler) so that the inner continuations stay inline (AwaitTaskContinuation.IsValidLocationForInlining). The handshake is AuthenticateAsClientAsync/AuthenticateAsServerAsync(options), begun where Java calls beginHandshake() or by the first wrap/unwrap; one SslStream.ReadAsync stays outstanding after it and a read of 0 is the peer's close_notify (Status.CLOSED), which below TLS 1.3 is answered with close_notify (EngineAcknowledgeCloseNotify: the JDK engine answers it itself, RFC 5246 7.2.1, SslStream does not, measured); a record shorter than its 5-byte header is BUFFER_UNDERFLOW without consuming input, as the JDK engine returns it; application data goes through WriteAsync once authenticated; closeOutbound() is ShutdownAsync (close_notify). Result status: pending output or an unreported failure is NEED_WRAP, a handshake waiting for input NEED_UNWRAP, a handshake that went on asynchronously NEED_TASK (resumed by SslTasksRunner when SslStream calls the mediation stream or completes an operation), a completed handshake Task FINISHED once. Failures are thrown once as AuthenticationException (SSLException): any other exception of the handshake Task (for example a CryptographicException thrown by a validation callback) or of a read/write is wrapped as its inner exception, as the JDK wraps a TrustManager's CertificateException in SSLHandshakeException. Public API: the SSLEngine constructors take SslClientAuthenticationOptions/SslServerAuthenticationOptions (+ startTls), owned by the handler; the Executor constructors, engine() (internal Engine() for the tests and SniHandler/OptionalSslHandler, which dispose it for a handler that never joined a pipeline; internal ClientOptions()/ServerOptions() give the tests the engine configuration), the package-private ResumptionController constructor (trust glue of the JDK engines, not ported) and the deprecated members are not ported; applicationProtocol() reads SslStream.NegotiatedApplicationProtocol (UTF-8, null when empty); handshakeFuture()/sslCloseFuture() are Task<IChannel> (TaskCompletionSource with RunContinuationsAsynchronously, LazyChannelPromise); closeOutbound()/closeOutbound(ChannelPromise) fold into Task CloseOutbound(); renegotiate()/renegotiate(Promise) are Renegotiate()/Renegotiate(TaskCompletionSource<IChannel>) (server: NegotiateClientCertificateAsync after ending the outstanding read; client: NotSupportedException, which fails and closes as a failing beginHandshake() does); (long, TimeUnit) setters take TimeSpan; the volatile longs use Volatile.Read/Write; the outbound operations are the Task-returning *Async overrides. Promises: the handler's own promises (aggregate write promises, the close_notify flush) complete their producers inline, cascades and listeners run on IdleStateHandler.ExecutorTaskScheduler(ctx) (at once on the event loop), the returned Tasks continue asynchronously as the Transport's do, and a queued write honours its CancellationToken. ignoreException(...) treats SocketException like IOException and replaces the StackTraceElement/class-loader walk with SocketErrorCode ConnectionReset/ConnectionAborted; the Java regex is a Regex with ASCII-only case folding and Java line terminators. Not ported because they only serve not-ported units (no comments): SslEngineType's TCNATIVE/CONSCRYPT branches (comments recorded), decodeNonJdkCompatible, setOpensslEngineSocketFd (UnixChannel fd for OpenSSL), AsyncTaskCompletionHandler (OpenSSL async tasks), toByteBuffer, inEventLoop(Executor), isIgnorableClassInStack and the resumption checks. Platform limits (CLR comments): renegotiation only as a server on freebsd/linux/windows; no close_notify before the handshake completes (ShutdownAsync needs an authenticated stream). Measured with scratch smoke tests on this host: TLS 1.2 and 1.3 handshakes, ALPN, 100 000 bytes both ways, close_notify, handshake timeout, startTls, NotSslRecordException, untrusted certificate, a throwing validation callback, server renegotiation (TLS 1.2 and 1.3), all on the calling thread.

Internal abstract subclass of the Transport AbstractCoalescingBufferQueue with an internal constructor; wrapDataSize() is the protected abstract WrapDataSize(); compose/composeFirst/removeEmptyValue override the Transport members. catch (Throwable) with PlatformDependent.throwException is catch (Exception) and throw;; assert is Debug.Assert; capacity() is the Capacity property and ensureWritableSuccess is ByteBufUtil.EnsureWritableSuccess.
Sealed subclass with the static readonly SUCCESS instance, a private success constructor and the public (Exception) constructor.

Sealed AuthenticationException with the reason constructor; SSLHandshakeException and SSLException map to the same type, so a handshake failure is not told apart from other SSL errors by type. javax.net.ssl.SSLException/SSLHandshakeException are System.Security.Authentication.AuthenticationException, the exception SslStream throws when the client or server cannot be authenticated (ssl design decision 3); AuthenticationException derives from SystemException, not IOException as SSLException does.

review.scope: Sealed class with the public const strings TLS_v1_2 and TLS_v1_3 and the private constructor with its comment. The @Deprecated SSL_v2_HELLO, SSL_v2, SSL_v3, TLS_v1 and TLS_v1_1, whose @deprecated text names TLS_v1_2/TLS_v1_3, are not ported (owner decision 2026-11-16); code that must name those protocols uses their text. Inside Netty.NET.Handler.Ssl the simple name SslProtocols binds to this class, not System.Security.Authentication.SslProtocols.

A Java enum with static methods is a sealed class with the static readonly instances JDK, OPENSSL and OPENSSL_REFCNT ([UnstableApi]) and ToString() returning the constant name, as codec-base Base64Dialect ports an enum with members (a C# enum cannot carry the static probes reached as SslProvider.isAlpnSupported(...)); the switch statements compare the instances and java.lang.Error is UnreachableException. SslStream is the only engine (owner decision 2026-11-24): JDK answers for it, isAlpnSupported(JDK) is true (SslStream takes ALPN lists as ApplicationProtocols; h2 negotiated in the design measurements), isTlsv13Supported(JDK) and isTlsv13EnabledByDefault(JDK) are SslUtils.IsTLSv13SupportedByJDK()/IsTLSv13EnabledByJDK() (wave-1 probes), isOptionSupported(JDK) is false; OPENSSL/OPENSSL_REFCNT answer false everywhere because OpenSsl is library-not-ported (owner decision 4). The java.security.Provider parameters have no counterpart: isTlsv13Supported(SslProvider, Provider) is not ported (its Javadoc equals the kept one-argument overload) and the internal isTlsv13EnabledByDefault has no Provider parameter. SslContextOption<?> is the non-generic SslContextOption.

Internal static class (The source's private constructor only prevents instantiation, so the class is static.) Record parsing is kept exactly: getEncryptedPacketLength(ByteBuf, int, boolean) reads the content type and major version with GetByte (the unsigned System.Byte, owner decision) and the version with the signed GetShort, compared with the DTLS constants, which are unchecked((short) 0xFEFF/0xFEFD/0xFEFC) so they keep their negative Java values; ByteBuf has no mutable byte order in this port, so unsignedShortBE/shortBE(ByteBuf) read big-endian without the order check. getEncryptedPacketLength(ByteBuffer[], int) takes ReadOnlyMemory<byte>[] (each element the position..limit region) and the private ByteBuffer overloads take ReadOnlySpan<byte> read big-endian with BinaryPrimitives; the five-byte header copy across buffers is a span copy. review.scope: javax.security.cert.X509Certificate, the JDK's deprecated-for-removal "Abstract class for X.509 v1 certificates", maps to the BCL base class X509Certificate, whose members cover the v1 attributes without the v3 extensions of X509Certificate2; its X509Certificate(X509Certificate) constructor is not obsolete. ChunkedWriteHandler matches any ChunkedInput<?>; B is covariant (out B), so every IChunkedInput<B> is an IChunkedInput<object> as the wildcard type is (covariance supports reference types only), and B has the class constraint because Java type arguments are reference types (as codec-base MessageAggregator). The @Deprecated readChunk(ChannelHandlerContext), whose @deprecated text names readChunk(ByteBufAllocator), is not ported (owner decision 2026-11-16) and its Javadoc is recorded as omitted; ByteBufAllocator is IByteBufAllocator.

Owner decision 5 (JVM-only NIO replaced without a facade): the FileChannel is a FileStream, the type the Transport DefaultFileRegion takes for a FileChannel, and File is FileInfo; new RandomAccessFile(in, "r").getChannel() opens a read-only FileStream. The positional FileChannel read ("does not modify this channel's position") is ByteBuf.WriteBytes(SafeFileHandle, long, int) on the stream's handle, the Buffer port's FileChannel overload (RandomAccess; the file position never changes), which reports the end of the file as 0 where FileChannel.read returns -1, so a non-positive count fails with EndOfStreamException (EOFException). isOpen() is FileStream.CanRead; size() is Length, read through a private Size() helper in the (FileStream, int) constructor so that a closed stream throws the Transport ClosedChannelException as FileChannel.size() does (Length of a closed FileStream throws ObjectDisposedException). review.scope: Simple Java enum: a C# enum with the same constants in declaration order; the constant Javadoc is kept.

state() and isFirst() keep their Java names as State() and IsFirst() (methods, not properties). IdleState is a C# enum, a value type, so ObjectUtil.checkNotNull(state, "state") has no counterpart. toString() uses StringUtil.SimpleClassName and the enum constant name, as the Java enum toString(); the private static final DefaultIdleStateEvent is a private sealed nested class.

A TimeSpan replaces each (long, TimeUnit) pair (docs/common-clr-design.md, "Monotonic time and duration conversion"), so the TimeUnit parameter and its checkNotNull have no counterpart; a positive TimeSpan converts to nanoseconds with saturation, as TimeUnit.toNanos does (MIN_TIMEOUT_NANOS is TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS.toNanos(1) = 1,000,000), and the nanosecond delays handed to the executor round up to the 100 ns TimeSpan tick, so a timeout task runs at most 99 ns after its Java deadline and never before it. The constructors (int, int, int) seconds, (TimeSpan, TimeSpan, TimeSpan) and (bool, TimeSpan, TimeSpan, TimeSpan) replace the TimeUnit overloads. Future<?> of the scheduled work is the CancellationTokenSource whose token was passed to ctx.Executor.ScheduleAsync (cancel(false) is Cancel()), as AbstractNioChannel keeps connectTimeoutFuture; the scheduled Task is not observed, as nothing observes the Java future. schedule(ctx, task, delay, unit), visible for testing, is the internal virtual Schedule(ctx, Action, TimeSpan) returning that CancellationTokenSource. The ticker is ctx.Executor.Ticker() as in Java (the EmbeddedChannel frozen clock in the tests). write(ctx, msg, promise) is WriteAsync and the Task returned by ctx.WriteAsync replaces the promise (docs/codec-base-porting.md, "Outbound operations"); there is no void promise to unvoid(). A write listener is a Task continuation on the TaskScheduler IdleStateHandler.ExecutorTaskScheduler over ctx.executor(): it runs at once when the write completes on the event loop and is otherwise handed to executor.execute, the policy of DefaultPromise.notifyListeners(). The write Tasks of the Transport port come from TaskCompletionSources with RunContinuationsAsynchronously ("Forces continuations added to the current task to be executed asynchronously"), so a continuation on TaskScheduler.Default would run later on a thread-pool thread; a continuation with its own scheduler is queued to that scheduler (QueueTask) by the completing thread. With TaskScheduler.Default, testWriterNotIdle, testAllNotIdle, testObserveWriterIdle and testObserveAllIdle failed in every run of this port. The listener field is assigned in the constructor (a field initializer cannot reference the instance, CS0236). Channel.Unsafe is folded into AbstractChannel, so unsafe().outboundBuffer() is (channel as AbstractChannel)?.OutboundBuffer (current(), totalPendingWriteBytes() and currentProgress() are the Current, TotalPendingWriteBytes and CurrentProgress properties); the Transport keeps a closed buffer instead of a null one, which the idle tasks never inspect because they return once the channel is closed. System.identityHashCode is RuntimeHelpers.GetHashCode (0 for null). The abstract Runnable AbstractIdleTask and its inner subclasses are nested classes with Run() that reach the handler through an explicit reference; catch (Throwable) is catch (Exception). newIdleStateEvent's message prints first as "true"/"false".
Sealed class as the final source class; INSTANCE is a static readonly shared instance; serialVersionUID has no counterpart.

ReadTimeoutHandler(long, TimeUnit) is ReadTimeoutHandler(TimeSpan) (see IdleStateHandler); the final channelIdle is a sealed override and its assert is Debug.Assert; ctx.close() discards the returned Task.

Extends the Transport ChannelException; the package-private constructors are internal and the shared constructor calls ChannelException(message, null, shared), which asserts shared as Java does. serialVersionUID has no counterpart. The fillInStackTrace() override, which returns this without recording frames, is an override of the virtual Exception.StackTrace that returns null ("If no stack trace is available ... the value is null"); its line comment stays with it.

Namespace Netty.NET.Handler.Traffic holds the ported types; the package summary ("Implementation of a Traffic Shaping Handler and Dynamic Statistics.

The main goal of this package is to allow you to shape the traffic (bandwidth limitation), but also to get statistics on how many bytes are read or written. Both functions can be active or inactive (traffic or statistics).

Two classes implement this behavior:

  • {@link io.netty.handler.traffic.TrafficCounter}: this class implements the counters needed by the handlers. It can be accessed to get some extra information like the read or write bytes since last check, the read and write bandwidth from last check...
  • {@link io.netty.handler.traffic.AbstractTrafficShapingHandler}: this abstract class implements the kernel of traffic shaping. It could be extended to fit your needs. Two classes are proposed as default implementations: see {@link io.netty.handler.traffic.ChannelTrafficShapingHandler} and {@link io.netty.handler.traffic.GlobalTrafficShapingHandler} respectively for Channel traffic shaping and global traffic shaping.

Both inbound and outbound traffic can be shaped independently. This is done by either passing in the desired limiting values to the constructors of both the Channel and Global traffic shaping handlers, or by calling the configure method on the {@link io.netty.handler.traffic.AbstractTrafficShapingHandler}. A value of 0 for either parameter indicates that there should be no limitation. This allows you to monitor the incoming and outgoing traffic without shaping.

To activate or deactivate the statistics, you can adjust the delay to a low (suggested not less than 200ms for efficiency reasons) or a high value (let say 24H in millisecond is huge enough to not get the problem) or even using 0 which means no computation will be done.

If you want to do anything with these statistics, just override the doAccounting method.
This interval can be changed either from the method configure in {@link io.netty.handler.traffic.AbstractTrafficShapingHandler} or directly using the method configure of {@link io.netty.handler.traffic.TrafficCounter}.

Note that a new {@link io.netty.handler.traffic.ChannelTrafficShapingHandler} must be created for each new channel, but only one {@link io.netty.handler.traffic.GlobalTrafficShapingHandler} must be created for all channels.

Note also that you can create different GlobalTrafficShapingHandler if you want to separate classes of channels (for instance either from business point of view or from bind address point of view).

The bootstrap API is asynchronous: newServer/newClient wait for BindAsync/ConnectAsync, writeAndFlush(...).sync(), close() and eventLoop().submit(...).get() are awaited, and the tests that await are async Task methods. The server binds the wildcard address as in Java; Java connects to the loopback address instead (SocketChannelImpl.checkRemote), while a CLR connect to 0.0.0.0 fails on Windows with SocketException "The requested address is not valid in its context" (observed), so newClient makes the same replacement. CountDownLatch is CountdownEvent with a countDown helper that ignores a zero count (Signal() throws there), LinkedBlockingQueue is ConcurrentQueue, AtomicInteger/AtomicReference are the Common types, and java.util.concurrent.Exchanger, which has no BCL counterpart, is a private two-party Monitor-based Exchanger with the timed exchange contract. testSwallowedReadComplete keeps the Java real-time Thread.sleep(delayMillis + 20) against the unfrozen EmbeddedChannel clock. readerIndex(int) is the ReaderIndex setter, refCnt() RefCnt, EMPTY_BUFFER EmptyBuffer; assertEquals(0, list.size()) is Assert.Empty (xUnit2013); calls take TestContext.Current.CancellationToken (xUnit1051).

One logging event is one IInternalLogger.Log(level, msg) call (Log(level, msg, cause) for exceptionCaught), so verify(appender).doAppend(argThat(matcher)) is Verify(Log(..., ArgThat(matcher)...), Times.Once()) with a Moq Match.Create custom matcher. caseMappings.adaptation: Ported 1:1. @BeforeAll/@AfterAll run from the class fixture BeforeAllAndAfterAll (docs/handler-porting.md, "Lifecycle"); @MethodSource is [MemberData]. SslProvider.values() is its three constants; OpenSsl is library-not-ported and reports unavailable, so expand(...) keeps the JDK/JDK pair. SslContext.newHandler(alloc, Executor) is not ported (no delegated tasks in SslStream), so expand(...) generates no delegate rows and the test, its newSslHandler helper and the ExecutorService have no executor. engine.getSupportedCipherSuites() is the set of TlsCipherSuite names (what JdkSslContext reports as supported); OpenSsl.isCipherSuiteAvailable answers false. CERT.getKeyPair().getPrivate() is the bundle's BCL key object (docs/pkitesting-porting.md). Promise<Object> is a TaskCompletionSource<object> (cancel(true) TrySetCanceled), await(5, SECONDS) is Task.WhenAny with a five-second delay. The test is skipped on Windows, where SslStream has no CipherSuitesPolicy (NewHandler throws PlatformNotSupportedException for configured cipher suites, docs/handler-ssl-design.md); it runs on Linux/macOS.

caseMappings.adaptation: Ported 1:1 (same method names, first letter upper case) on Netty.NET.Handler.Ssl, whose SslHandler drives System.Net.Security.SslStream (owner decisions 2026-11-24, docs/handler-ssl-design.md). An SSLEngine of SSLContext.getDefault() is the SslClientAuthenticationOptions/SslServerAuthenticationOptions that SslHandler(options) takes (a JDK engine without setUseClientMode is in server mode, TransportContext "new SSLConfiguration(sslContext, false)"), SSLException/SSLHandshakeException/SSLProtocolException are AuthenticationException (ssl design decision 3), CertificateException/SignatureException are CryptographicException (ssl wave 1), and the session facts of engine().getSession() come from the internal SslHandler.Engine() (SslStream). The tests that used the @Deprecated CachedSelfSignedCertificate/SelfSignedCertificate (not ported, recorded by the lead) use a nested SelfSignedCertificateBundle that caches the X509Bundle that SelfSignedCertificate's CertificateBuilderCertGenerator builds by default (self-signed CA "CN=localhost", RSA 2048): certificate()/privateKey() are its PEM files (ToTempCertChainPem/ToTempPrivateKeyPem), cert() its certificate and key() its BCL key object (docs/pkitesting-porting.md). ChannelFuture/ChannelPromise/Promise/Future are Task/TaskCompletionSource (sync()/syncUninterruptibly() awaits, await()/awaitUninterruptibly() awaits with ConfigureAwaitOptions.SuppressThrowing | ContinueOnCapturedContext (xUnit1030), cause() a CauseOf helper, isSuccess() IsCompletedSuccessfully); the bootstrap API is asynchronous (BindAsync/ConnectAsync), new InetSocketAddress(0) is the wildcard IPEndPoint and the clients connect to it through the loopback address as the JDK does (docs/handler-porting.md, "Socket tests"). @Timeout(value, MILLISECONDS) is the Timeout of the [Fact]/[Theory] (async tests; a test whose helper waits with TestContext.Current.CancellationToken disables xUnit1069 with a reason), CountDownLatch is CountdownEvent with a CountDown helper that ignores a zero count, LinkedBlockingQueue is BlockingCollection (take() Take, poll(timeout) TryTake), ConcurrentLinkedQueue ConcurrentQueue, AtomicBoolean/AtomicReference the Common types, Thread.sleep Task.Delay, (long, TimeUnit) TimeSpan, and anonymous classes are named nested classes. OpenSSL/Conscrypt providers and tests are library-not-ported (owner decision 2026-11-24). data() keeps the JDK rows (TLSv1.2, TLSv1.3); the OPENSSL rows and their OpenSsl.isAvailable() assumption are dropped (library-not-ported). @Timeout(30) seconds is Timeout = 30000 ms (xUnit1069 disabled: the EmbeddedChannel body has no wait). The event queues are ConcurrentQueue<object> (poll() is TryDequeue), MERGE_CUMULATOR is ByteToMessageDecoder.MERGE_CUMULATOR, US_ASCII is Encoding.ASCII, outboundMessages().peek()/poll() are TryPeek/Dequeue, and engine().getSession().getProtocol() is SslHandler.Engine().SslProtocol turned into the JSSE name. "make sure client automatically responds with close_notify" on TLS 1.2 needed the SslHandler fix of this wave: SslStream does not answer a received close_notify (measured), the JDK engine does below TLS 1.3 (TransportContext.passiveInboundClose, RFC 5246 7.2.1), so EngineAcknowledgeCloseNotify closes the outbound side.

notApplicableMethods.reason: The test subclasses javax.net.ssl.TrustManagerFactory with a TrustManagerFactorySpi whose engineGetTrustManagers() returns null and checks that the null array does not reach the trust manager wrapping of the JDK context (wrapIfNeeded/wrapTrustManagerIfNeeded, issue 14488). The TrustManagerFactory is an X509ChainPolicy (owner decision 2026-11-24, ssl design decision 3), which has no trust manager array and no SPI, and the wrapping it guards (EnhancingX509ExtendedTrustManager, ResumptionController) is jvm-only-replaced, so the case cannot be built; the platform-default trust of a context without a policy is JdkSslContext's null CertificateChainPolicy.

review.scope: Every ported JUnit method is a [Fact] or [Theory] with the same name (first letter upper case); the anonymous classes are named nested classes and asserts with messages use XunitAssertMessages.AssertM. notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: A server JdkAlpnApplicationProtocolNegotiator with a custom ProtocolSelectorFactory that selects a protocol the client did not offer (JdkSslServerContext/JdkSslClientContext, TestDelegatingSslContext setting the engine protocols and cipher suites): the client handshake fails or the channel closes.
notApplicableMethods.reason: The JdkApplicationProtocolNegotiator/JdkAlpnApplicationProtocolNegotiator, JdkSslServerContext and JdkSslClientContext types are @Deprecated with replacements named (ApplicationProtocolConfig, SslContextBuilder) and not ported (lead decision); ApplicationProtocolConfig has no selector, SslStream selects the server protocol itself from the client list, and TestDelegatingSslContext.initEngine needs the SSLEngine (DelegatingSslContext.initEngine is jvm-only-replaced).

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: SSLEngineTest.testEnablingAnAlreadyDisabledSslProtocol(param, {}, {TLSv1.2}): setEnabledProtocols on an engine of newEngine and getEnabledProtocols.
notApplicableMethods.reason: No SSLEngine facade (owner decision 2026-11-24, docs/handler-ssl-design.md): SslHandler drives an SslStream whose options it creates and keeps, and SslStream exposes no wrap/unwrap ("Data moves through the engine by calling wrap() or unwrap()", SSLEngine Javadoc), no handshake status or delegated tasks, no closeInbound/closeOutbound/isInboundDone/isOutboundDone, no enabled/supported protocol or cipher suite lists, no SSLParameters and no SSLSession/SSLSessionContext (its members are listed on the SslStream page). SslStream has no engine-level protocol list (the protocols are the options' EnabledSslProtocols, set by the context).

review.scope: The JDK fixture of SSLEngineTest on SslStream. ProviderType is a sealed class with ALPN_JAVA only (ALPN_CONSCRYPT is library-not-ported); its JCA Provider and the provider hooks are not ported; JdkAlpnSslUtils.supportsAlpn() is SslProvider.IsAlpnSupported(JDK). @MethodSource("newJdkParams") is [MemberData] over a static NewJdkParams(); TestAbortedException is Assert.Skip. The @Disabled overrides of testMutualAuthValidClientCertChainTooLong* override the virtual bodies that the SSLEngineTest theories call (the theory declarations are in SSLEngineTest.cs) and skip with the @Disabled comment. mySetupMutualAuthServerIsValidException keeps the causedBySSLException work-around.
Ported 1:1: the JDK subclass of RenegotiateTest overrides ServerSslProvider() with SslProvider.JDK (SslStream); it declares no test of its own and runs the inherited TestRenegotiateServer.

notApplicableMethods.reason: The test calls the package-private JdkSslServerContext.checkIfWrappingTrustManagerIsSupported(), which asks whether the JDK lets the @Deprecated server context wrap its X509ExtendedTrustManager in an EnhancingX509ExtendedTrustManager; JdkSslServerContext is deprecated-not-ported and EnhancingX509ExtendedTrustManager jvm-only-replaced (SslStream reports a host name mismatch as SslPolicyErrors.RemoteCertificateNameMismatch).
notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: JdkSslServerContext.checkIfWrappingTrustManagerIsSupported() does not throw.

notApplicableMethods.reason: The test subclasses javax.net.ssl.TrustManagerFactory with a TrustManagerFactorySpi whose engineGetTrustManagers() returns null and checks that the null array does not reach the trust manager wrapping of the JDK context (wrapIfNeeded/wrapTrustManagerIfNeeded, issue 14488). The TrustManagerFactory is an X509ChainPolicy (owner decision 2026-11-24, ssl design decision 3), which has no trust manager array and no SPI, and the wrapping it guards (EnhancingX509ExtendedTrustManager, ResumptionController) is jvm-only-replaced, so the case cannot be built; the platform-default trust of a context without a policy is JdkSslContext's null CertificateChainPolicy. It also uses the @Deprecated SelfSignedCertificate.
notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: Building a server context with a TrustManagerFactory whose getTrustManagers() returns null does not throw.

review.scope: Every ported JUnit method is a [Fact] or [Theory] with the same name (first letter upper case); the anonymous classes are named nested classes and asserts with messages use XunitAssertMessages.AssertM. The @Deprecated JdkSslClientContext/JdkSslServerContext constructors ("@deprecated Use {@link SslContextBuilder} to create {@link JdkSslContext} instances and only use {@link JdkSslContext} in your code.") are not ported, so newSslContext builds the same context with SslContextBuilder and the JDK provider. newSslContext is SslContextBuilder.forServer(File, File, String). The inherited SslContextTest tests run for this class.

notPorted.reason: The class plugs a signature implementation into the JCA (java.security.Provider) for the OpenSSL private-key-method test. Its only user, JdkDelegatingPrivateKeyMethodTest, is library-not-ported (netty-tcnative), as is the JdkDelegatingPrivateKeyMethod it tests; no ported unit delegates handshake signatures (SslStream signs with the certificate key of the platform TLS stack).

caseMappings.adaptation: Every ported JUnit method is a [Fact] or [Theory] with the same name (first letter upper case); the anonymous classes are named nested classes and asserts with messages use XunitAssertMessages.AssertM. Mockito is Moq: the @Mock fields are Mock<T> fields (MockitoAnnotations.initMocks has no counterpart), @BeforeEach setUp() runs from the constructor, verify(...) is Verify and verifyNoInteractions is VerifyNoOtherCalls; Mockito.mock(SslHandler.class) is a Mock<SslHandler> built with server authentication options. The tests call the protected decode(...) through Java package access; C# protected access is limited to derived classes, so the handlers are nested OptionalSslHandler subclasses with an InvokeDecode forwarder (MqttDecoder records the same constraint). "plaintext".getBytes() is Encoding.Default (docs/codec-stomp-porting.md).

caseMappings.adaptation: Ported 1:1 (same method names, first letter upper case) on Netty.NET.Handler.Ssl, whose SslHandler drives System.Net.Security.SslStream (owner decisions 2026-11-24, docs/handler-ssl-design.md). An SSLEngine of SSLContext.getDefault() is the SslClientAuthenticationOptions/SslServerAuthenticationOptions that SslHandler(options) takes (a JDK engine without setUseClientMode is in server mode, TransportContext "new SSLConfiguration(sslContext, false)"), SSLException/SSLHandshakeException/SSLProtocolException are AuthenticationException (ssl design decision 3), CertificateException/SignatureException are CryptographicException (ssl wave 1), and the session facts of engine().getSession() come from the internal SslHandler.Engine() (SslStream). caseMappings.adaptation: Every ported JUnit method is a [Fact] or [Theory] with the same name (first letter upper case); the anonymous classes are named nested classes and asserts with messages use XunitAssertMessages.AssertM. PrivateKey is AsymmetricAlgorithm and getEncoded() its virtual ExportPkcs8PrivateKey(), so the anonymous PrivateKey whose getEncoded() returns null is a nested AsymmetricAlgorithm whose override returns null; PemPrivateKey.toPEM is internal.

notApplicableMethods.reason: The test builds a server context from a PemPrivateKey/PemX509Certificate with SslProvider.OPENSSL after OpenSsl.ensureAvailability() and asserts it is a ReferenceCountedOpenSslContext; OpenSSL (netty-tcnative) is library-not-ported (owner decision 2026-11-24, docs/handler-ssl-design.md decision 3): OpenSsl.isAvailable() is false and SslProvider.OPENSSL/OPENSSL_REFCNT cannot be built (SslContext.newServerContextInternal/newClientContextInternal throw NotSupportedException).

caseMappings.adaptation: The abstract fixture runs through its only concrete fixture JdkSslEngineTest (xUnit runs the theories of an abstract base class for each derived class). Ported: the 14 tests that run through SslContext, SslHandler and a NIO socket pipeline (mutual auth with key files and PKCS #12 key stores, client host name validation, client-initiated renegotiation, testInvalidCipher, testRSASSAPSS); the 51 tests that drive an SSLEngine (wrap/unwrap handshakes, engine state, SSLSession/SSLSessionContext, trust/key manager callbacks with handshake sessions, session resumption, master key logging, the peer certificate chain) are CLR-inapplicable, and SSLEngineTest.NotApplicable.cs keeps their original comments in source order. Fixture: @TestInstance(PER_CLASS) with @BeforeEach/@AfterEach is IAsyncLifetime InitializeAsync/DisposeAsync; @MethodSource("newTestParams") is [MemberData] over a static NewTestParams() (xUnit member data is a public static member), which asks SslProvider.IsTlsv13Supported(JDK) as the constructor flag did; the delegate=true parameters (newHandler(alloc, Executor), jvm-only-replaced) and DelayingExecutor are not used; the JCA Provider hooks and sslContextProvider are not ported; SelfSignedCertificate/CachedSelfSignedCertificate (@Deprecated) are pkitesting CertificateBuilder bundles built as CertificateBuilderCertGenerator builds them. newEngine + new SslHandler(engine) is SslContext.NewHandler (the handler owns the SslStream options): the server engine's setNeedClientAuth(true) is ClientAuth.REQUIRE on the context and the client engine's setNeedClientAuth(true) has no counterpart; the client engine's SSLParameters (endpoint identification HTTPS) are set on the client context; SSLSession facts are the SslStream of SslHandler.Engine() (LocalCertificate, RemoteCertificate, NegotiatedCipherSuite against the context's cipher suites because SslStream applies no Netty cipher order, SslProtocol as the JSSE name; id/times/isValid/getPeerCertificateChain have no member); the JDK 9 ALPN accessor is NegotiatedApplicationProtocol. KeyStore.load + KeyManagerFactory.init are SslContext.BuildKeyManagerFactory over the PKCS #12 bytes. Measured platform adaptations: the wildcard bind is IPv6Any on the dual-mode Transport socket (the JDK binds the IPv6 wildcard for 0.0.0.0); the expired trusted resources (mutual_auth_ca.pem 2017, test2.crt 2014) are accepted by JdkSslContext, which, like PKIX, does not check the validity of trust anchors (RFC 5280 6.1, 6.1.3) where the Windows chain engine reports NotTimeValid; in testClientHostnameValidationFail the server handshake completes before SslStream verifies the server certificate on the client (SslStream.IO.cs CompleteHandshake), so the server waits for the failure that follows; clientInitiatedRenegotiationWithFatalAlertDoesNotInfiniteLoopServer calls Assert.Skip on Windows (its contexts configure cipher suites and Windows has no CipherSuitesPolicy). testMutualAuthValidClientCertChainTooLong* call a virtual body that JdkSslEngineTest overrides (its @Disabled). SSLException/SSLHandshakeException are AuthenticationException; CountDownLatch is CountdownEvent; BlockingQueue is BlockingCollection/ConcurrentQueue; the anonymous handlers are named nested classes.

The server records no error for its handshake success when a failure is expected: SslStream verifies the server certificate after the handshake loop (SslStream.IO.cs: CompleteHandshake "Optionally verifies the Remote Certificate" after the loop and then sends its alert), so the server handshake completes and its failure is the read of the client's alert (AuthenticationException, measured TLSv1.2/1.3); the pending client write fails with the same exception object as the handshake (Assert.Same). The client trust file is the X509ChainPolicy adaptation of the expired NettyTestRoot (see the entry).

Ported with Assert.Skip on Windows: the contexts configure param.ciphers(), and SslContext.NewHandler throws PlatformNotSupportedException there (no CipherSuitesPolicy, docs/handler-ssl-design.md). The client renegotiate() of SslHandler fails at once with NotSupportedException (SslStream renegotiates only as a server), which closes the client, so the server becomes inactive without a renegotiation loop (measured without cipher suites: inactive within 15 ms for all six parameters). assumeTrue(Java >= 11) has no counterpart; [Theory(Timeout = 30000)] is @Timeout(30).

SSLSocketFactory default cipher suites are SslUtils.DEFAULT_CIPHER_SUITES (SslStream lists none); newEngine is NewHandler, which rejects "InvalidCipher" with ArgumentException before the CipherSuitesPolicy would be created, on every platform; the SslStream of the handler that never joined a pipeline is disposed through Engine().

notApplicableMethods.sourceContract: TLSv1.2 parameters only: setEnabledCipherSuites on a client and a server engine of newEngine and getEnabledCipherSuites returns exactly that suite.
notApplicableMethods.reason: No SSLEngine facade (owner decision 2026-11-24, docs/handler-ssl-design.md): SslHandler drives an SslStream whose options it creates and keeps, and SslStream exposes no wrap/unwrap ("Data moves through the engine by calling wrap() or unwrap()", SSLEngine Javadoc), no handshake status or delegated tasks, no closeInbound/closeOutbound/isInboundDone/isOutboundDone, no enabled/supported protocol or cipher suite lists, no SSLParameters and no SSLSession/SSLSessionContext (its members are listed on the SslStream page). The test drives SSLEngine.setEnabledCipherSuites/getEnabledCipherSuites directly, so it has no SslHandler/SslStream counterpart (a test whose subject is a JSSE-only member is CLR-inapplicable).

review.scope: The abstract fixture runs through its only concrete fixture JdkSslEngineTest (xUnit runs the theories of an abstract base class for each derived class). Ported: the 14 tests that run through SslContext, SslHandler and a NIO socket pipeline (mutual auth with key files and PKCS #12 key stores, client host name validation, client-initiated renegotiation, testInvalidCipher, testRSASSAPSS); the 51 tests that drive an SSLEngine (wrap/unwrap handshakes, engine state, SSLSession/SSLSessionContext, trust/key manager callbacks with handshake sessions, session resumption, master key logging, the peer certificate chain) are CLR-inapplicable, and SSLEngineTest.NotApplicable.cs keeps their original comments in source order. Fixture: @TestInstance(PER_CLASS) with @BeforeEach/@AfterEach is IAsyncLifetime InitializeAsync/DisposeAsync; @MethodSource("newTestParams") is [MemberData] over a static NewTestParams() (xUnit member data is a public static member), which asks SslProvider.IsTlsv13Supported(JDK) as the constructor flag did; the delegate=true parameters (newHandler(alloc, Executor), jvm-only-replaced) and DelayingExecutor are not used; the JCA Provider hooks and sslContextProvider are not ported; SelfSignedCertificate/CachedSelfSignedCertificate (@Deprecated) are pkitesting CertificateBuilder bundles built as CertificateBuilderCertGenerator builds them. newEngine + new SslHandler(engine) is SslContext.NewHandler (the handler owns the SslStream options): the server engine's setNeedClientAuth(true) is ClientAuth.REQUIRE on the context and the client engine's setNeedClientAuth(true) has no counterpart; the client engine's SSLParameters (endpoint identification HTTPS) are set on the client context; SSLSession facts are the SslStream of SslHandler.Engine() (LocalCertificate, RemoteCertificate, NegotiatedCipherSuite against the context's cipher suites because SslStream applies no Netty cipher order, SslProtocol as the JSSE name; id/times/isValid/getPeerCertificateChain have no member); the JDK 9 ALPN accessor is NegotiatedApplicationProtocol. KeyStore.load + KeyManagerFactory.init are SslContext.BuildKeyManagerFactory over the PKCS #12 bytes. Measured platform adaptations: the wildcard bind is IPv6Any on the dual-mode Transport socket (the JDK binds the IPv6 wildcard for 0.0.0.0); the expired trusted resources (mutual_auth_ca.pem 2017, test2.crt 2014) are accepted by JdkSslContext, which, like PKIX, does not check the validity of trust anchors (RFC 5280 6.1, 6.1.3) where the Windows chain engine reports NotTimeValid; in testClientHostnameValidationFail the server handshake completes before SslStream verifies the server certificate on the client (SslStream.IO.cs CompleteHandshake), so the server waits for the failure that follows; clientInitiatedRenegotiationWithFatalAlertDoesNotInfiniteLoopServer calls Assert.Skip on Windows (its contexts configure cipher suites and Windows has no CipherSuitesPolicy). testMutualAuthValidClientCertChainTooLong* call a virtual body that JdkSslEngineTest overrides (its @Disabled). SSLException/SSLHandshakeException are AuthenticationException; CountDownLatch is CountdownEvent; BlockingQueue is BlockingCollection/ConcurrentQueue; the anonymous handlers are named nested classes.

The options are private state of SslHandler (engine() is internal and returns the SslStream, which does not expose them), so the tests read its serverOptions field through reflection (Type.GetField with BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Instance), as the Buffer tests read private allocator state. closeInbound/closeOutbound/release of an engine that never handshook is Engine().Dispose() of the handler's SslStream (as SniHandler releases one). The @Deprecated JdkSslClientContext/JdkSslServerContext constructors ("@deprecated Use {@link SslContextBuilder} to create {@link JdkSslContext} instances and only use {@link JdkSslContext} in your code.") are not ported, so newSslContext builds the same context with SslContextBuilder and the JDK provider. The deprecated constructors wrapped an unreadable key in SSLException; SslContextBuilder.keyManager(File, File, String)/forServer(File, File, String) report it as IllegalArgumentException ("File does not contain valid private key: ...", as the Java builder does), so the expectation is ArgumentException whose InnerException is the CryptographicException.

caseMappings.adaptation: Ported 1:1 (same method names, first letter upper case) on Netty.NET.Handler.Ssl, whose SslHandler drives System.Net.Security.SslStream (owner decisions 2026-11-24, docs/handler-ssl-design.md). An SSLEngine of SSLContext.getDefault() is the SslClientAuthenticationOptions/SslServerAuthenticationOptions that SslHandler(options) takes (a JDK engine without setUseClientMode is in server mode, TransportContext "new SSLConfiguration(sslContext, false)"), SSLException/SSLHandshakeException/SSLProtocolException are AuthenticationException (ssl design decision 3), CertificateException/SignatureException are CryptographicException (ssl wave 1), and the session facts of engine().getSession() come from the internal SslHandler.Engine() (SslStream). The tests that used the @Deprecated CachedSelfSignedCertificate/SelfSignedCertificate (not ported, recorded by the lead) use a nested SelfSignedCertificateBundle that caches the X509Bundle that SelfSignedCertificate's CertificateBuilderCertGenerator builds by default (self-signed CA "CN=localhost", RSA 2048): certificate()/privateKey() are its PEM files (ToTempCertChainPem/ToTempPrivateKeyPem), cert() its certificate and key() its BCL key object (docs/pkitesting-porting.md). ChannelFuture/ChannelPromise/Promise/Future are Task/TaskCompletionSource (sync()/syncUninterruptibly() awaits, await()/awaitUninterruptibly() awaits with ConfigureAwaitOptions.SuppressThrowing | ContinueOnCapturedContext (xUnit1030), cause() a CauseOf helper, isSuccess() IsCompletedSuccessfully); the bootstrap API is asynchronous (BindAsync/ConnectAsync), new InetSocketAddress(0) is the wildcard IPEndPoint and the clients connect to it through the loopback address as the JDK does (docs/handler-porting.md, "Socket tests"). @Timeout(value, MILLISECONDS) is the Timeout of the [Fact]/[Theory] (async tests; a test whose helper waits with TestContext.Current.CancellationToken disables xUnit1069 with a reason), CountDownLatch is CountdownEvent with a CountDown helper that ignores a zero count, LinkedBlockingQueue is BlockingCollection (take() Take, poll(timeout) TryTake), ConcurrentLinkedQueue ConcurrentQueue, AtomicBoolean/AtomicReference the Common types, Thread.sleep Task.Delay, (long, TimeUnit) TimeSpan, and anonymous classes are named nested classes. OpenSSL/Conscrypt providers and tests are library-not-ported (owner decision 2026-11-24). Per test: the anonymous SslHandler/EmbeddedChannel/handler subclasses are nested classes (the isActive() override reads a flag set from a primary-constructor parameter before the base constructor runs); ch.write(msg).get() is the awaited Task, which throws the UnsupportedMessageTypeException itself (no ExecutionException); the duplex handler of testNonApplicationDataFailureFailsQueuedWrites returns a TaskCompletionSource Task as the write promise. A server-mode SSLEngine of the default SSLContext has no key material, while SslStream refuses a server without certificate when authentication starts (NotSupportedException "The server mode SSL must use a certificate with the associated private key", measured), so newServerModeSSLEngine() carries the cached test certificate as ServerCertificateContext. SslProtocols.SSL_v3 (deprecated, not ported) is its text "SSLv3". The connect listener that writes "before fireChannelActive is called" (testHandshakeFailedByWriteBeforeChannelActive, testHandshakeTimeoutFlushStartsHandshake) is a first handler that writes from channelActive before passing the event on, because the Transport's connect Task runs its continuations asynchronously (docs/handler-porting.md, "Listener timing"); AssertionError is UnreachableException. testHandshakeFailBeforeWritePromise runs its write listener on IdleStateHandler.ExecutorTaskScheduler(ctx) (at once on the event loop, as DefaultPromise does) so the failed write precedes the close event (a thread-pool continuation raced with it, measured). The X509ExtendedTrustManager of testHandshakeFailureOnlyFireExceptionOnce is a RemoteCertificateValidationCallback returning false (a trust manager rejects by throwing CertificateException, which JSSE turns into an alert; a callback rejects by returning false, after which SslStream sends the fatal alert, while an exception thrown by the callback propagates without one, SslStream.Protocol.cs). Adapted assertions (measured SslStream behaviour, CLR comments): testIncompleteWriteDoesNotCompletePromisePrematurely asserts finishAndReleaseAll() false, because SslStream writes no user_canceled/close_notify alert for a handshake closed before it completed; testHandshakeFailureOnlyFireExceptionOnce asserts that the server handshake succeeded, because SslStream validates the server certificate after its handshake completed, and the client's alert then fails the server's first read (the single DecoderException). testHandshakeFailureCipherMissmatch* skip on Windows (CipherSuitesPolicy unsupported, NewHandler throws PlatformNotSupportedException). testIncorrectLength relies on the SslHandler fix of this wave (a record shorter than the 5-byte header is BUFFER_UNDERFLOW, as in the JDK engine). The not-applicable tests' original comments are kept in CLR comment blocks at their places.
